title: Backward-compatible adapter and unified pagination mapping for embeddings/rerank
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Multiple client integrations (old SDKs + third‑party mirrors) rely on differing embeddings/rerank response shapes, cursor tokens, and HTTP error semantics. This causes brittle pagination, inconsistent retry behavior, and sporadic 500s surfaced as 400s in downstream tooling. Goal: Ship a server-side adapter and client polyfill guidance that normalizes cursor shapes, maps internal error classes to stable HTTP codes, and provides a short-lived compatibility shim while we converge official SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Server exposes a /compat/embeddings-rerank endpoint that accepts legacy request parameters (cursor, page_token, limit) and returns the unified cursor format (next_cursor) used by new clients.

Error mapping matrix is documented and implemented: transient infra errors => 502/503, rate limits => 429 with Retry-After, client contract violations => 400 with structured error body, authentication issues => 401/403.
Backward adapter preserves KV cache semantics (no cache poisoning) and does not increase tail latency by >10% on p99 in performance tests.
SDK polyfill examples (JS + Python) demonstrating translation of legacy cursor -> canonical cursor and transparent retry logic are published in the SDK repo.
Integration tests cover edge cases: empty result pages, duplicated IDs across pages, cursor-expiry handling, and racey cursor invalidation during concurrent reads.
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Decided to implement a server-side compatibility adapter rather than forcing client migrations immediately to minimize outage risk. (PM + ENG + DX)
2026-03-04: Selected canonical cursor shape: base64-encoded JSON containing {v:2, sid:<session>, idx:<offset>, checksum:<sha1>} to tolerate future fields without breaking older parsers.

2026-03-06: Error semantics: agreed to map internal retriable errors to 502/503 and not conflate them with validation 4xxs. Decided to include structured error.code rationales for easier client mapping.
2026-03-08: Trade-off: adapter will add a 1–3 ms header decode/encode step; acceptable vs forced migrations across hundreds of customers.
implementation_notes: Adapter lives behind routing rule: requests with legacy header X-Redwood-Compat: emb-rank -> /compat/embeddings-rerank handler.
Handler responsibilities: normalize request params, translate cursor formats, enforce max_page_limit=100, and call core embeddings/rerank pipeline with canonical contract.
Cursor format chosen to be extensible and verifiable (version tag + checksum) to avoid sticky client parsing bugs and allow graceful rotation.
Add a targeted feature flag to enable adapter per-tenant for staged rollout and fast rollback.
Performance: implement the cursor translation in the routing layer using a tiny fastparse routine to keep p99 overhead minimal; avoid heavyweight JSON parsing where possible.
Add metrics: compat_adapter.requests, compat_adapter.latency_p50/p95/p99, compat_adapter.cursor_errors, compat_adapter.cache_misses.
Security: ensure adapter does not increase token exposure; do not log raw cursor payloads.
test_plan: Unit tests for cursor encoder/decoder including tampered checksum detection and version fallback behavior.
Integration tests exercising both legacy and new client shapes against the adapter in staging with synthetic and live-like datasets.
Chaos test: simulate intermittent backend 5xxs and verify adapter surface maps correct HTTP codes and Retry-After when appropriate.
Load test at target throughput for Dedicated customers to measure p99 impact (goal: <10% regression).
E2E golden tests: sample customer flows that previously failed due to mismatched cursor semantics.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Enable adapter for internal tenants only, run integration tests, validate metrics and logs. (2 days)
Phase 2 (canary): Enable adapter for 10% of traffic for a subset of low-latency customers; monitor compat_adapter.* metrics and customer error dashboards. (3 days)
Phase 3 (tenant opt-in): Offer adapter toggle in Console for customers to opt in; collect feedback and SDK telemetry. (1 week)
Phase 4 (graduation): Flip default to ON for all hosted tenants while continuing to provide deprecation guidance for legacy client parameters. (2 weeks)
Rollback: Feature flag removed or route disabled if >2x baseline error rate or >15% p99 latency regression observed.
